target.title: fix(active-memory): normalize legacy toggle timestamps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Active Memory doctor migration accepted any numeric legacy `updatedAt` value. JSON overflow values can parse to `Infinity`, which would be imported into plugin state instead of being normalized.

## Why This Change Was Made

The migration now accepts only finite legacy timestamps and falls back to `Date.now()` for malformed values, matching the existing fallback behavior for non-number timestamps.

## User Impact

Doctor migration no longer writes non-finite timestamps into Active Memory session-toggle state. Valid finite timestamps are preserved.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-vitest-cache-active-memory-doctor-reviewfix node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/active-memory/doctor-contract-api.test.ts`

- `git diff --check`
- Claude autoreview: clean after review fix and rebase to `upstream/main`

## Proof

The regression test writes a raw legacy JSON file with `updatedAt: 1e999`, verifies the migration imports the toggle, and proves the imported timestamp is the fixed `Date.now()` value rather than a non-finite number.

target.title: fix(web-fetch): recover from stale runtime providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Runtime web-fetch metadata can retain a selected provider id that is no longer available in the current provider list. When the user did not explicitly configure that provider, resolution returned no provider instead of falling back to the current auto-detected provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resolver now treats an explicit `providerId` as authoritative and fail-closed, while allowing stale runtime `selectedProvider` metadata to fall back to auto-detection. This keeps explicit config strict without letting old runtime state disable web fetch.

## User Impact

Users recover web fetch automatically after provider metadata becomes stale, while invalid explicit provider configuration still fails clearly.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-vitest-cache-web-content-rebase node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/web-content-core/src/provider-runtime-shared.test.ts`

target.body: ## Summary `agent.identity.get` returned inline data URIs for workspace-relative avatars, but the **Control UI Personal card** is initialized from the **bootstrap config** (`control-ui-config.json`), which still mapped workspace avatars through `resolveAssistantAvatarUrl` to the auth-gated `/avatar/` route. An `` tag cannot carry a Bearer header, so the linked Personal-card 401/broken-image symptom persisted despite the RPC fix. This PR consolidates the workspace-safe avatar reader into **one shared, gateway-internal helper** (`readLocalAvatarDataUrl` in `session-utils.ts`) and uses it in **both** projections — `agent.identity.get` and the bootstrap config handler — so identity and bootstrap produce identical inline data URIs. Remote HTTP URLs, existing data URLs, text fallbacks, and the `/avatar/` HTTP endpoint are unchanged. The helper is **not** re-exported on the Plugin SDK surface (`session-utils.ts` is gateway-internal; the `identity-avatar` barrel does not re-export it). The workspace root is canonicalised with `realpathSync` to keep the containment check correct for symlinked workspaces. Fixes #97602. ## What Problem This Solves The Personal card in Control UI showed a broken avatar image because its avatar comes from the bootstrap config, not from `agent.identity.get`: - UI chat avatar → `agent.identity.get` (already fixed in the first revision). - **Config Personal card** → `appConfig.assistantIdentity.avatar` → bootstrap `control-ui-config.json` → `/avatar/` (auth-gated → `` 401). **This PR fixes this path.** Given a workspace with an avatar file `avatar.png`: - **Before**: bootstrap `assistantAvatar` = `/avatar/main` (route URL → `` 401) - **After**: bootstrap `assistantAvatar` = `data:image/png;base64,...` (inline → renders) ## Why This Change Was Made ClawSweeper's P1: the earlier fix covered only `agent.identity.get`, leaving the bootstrap Personal-card path emitting the protected route. Rather than duplicate a third avatar reader, this revision lands **one canonical projection**: 1. `readLocalAvatarDataUrl(filePath, workspaceDir)` moves from `agent.ts` into `session-utils.ts` (exported gateway-internal, off the SDK barrel). 2. `agent.identity.get` imports the shared helper (behaviour unchanged). 3. The bootstrap config handler resolves the avatar via the same `resolveAgentAvatar(...)` and, when `kind === "local"`, inlines the file with the shared helper before `resolveAssistantAvatarUrl` (which passes data URIs through untouched). On any failure it falls back to the route URL. ## Changes - `src/gateway/session-utils.ts`: add exported gateway-internal `readLocalAvatarDataUrl` (shared reader). - `src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts`: import the shared helper; remove the now-duplicated private copy and its now-unused imports. - `src/gateway/control-ui.ts`: inline workspace-local avatars as data URIs in the bootstrap config response. - `src/gateway/control-ui.http.test.ts`: bootstrap-config regression test asserting a workspace-local avatar is returned as a data URI (not `/avatar/main`). ## Evidence **1. Real behavior proof — standalone harness driving the real `handleControlUiHttpRequest` bootstrap path** A standalone script (not a committed test) creates a real workspace with a real `avatar.png`, invokes the production bootstrap-config handler, and prints the `assistantAvatar` from the actual JSON response body: ``` ========== BEFORE (PR head control-ui.ts) ========== handled: true assistantAvatar (first 48 chars): "/avatar/main" startsWith 'data:image/png;base64,' -> false contains '/avatar/main' (broken auth-gated route) -> true ========== AFTER (fix) ========== handled: true assistantAvatar (first 48 chars): "data:image/png;base64,YXZhdGFyLWJ5dGVzCg==" startsWith 'data:image/png;base64,' -> true contains '/avatar/main' (broken auth-gated route) -> false ``` **3. target.title: fix(mattermost): backfill thread history from server when in-memory window is empty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost users replying in an existing thread could lose earlier thread context after the OpenClaw monitor restarted or the agent session was reset.

Fixes #93204

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost monitor now backfills a cold local thread-history window from the Mattermost thread endpoint after inbound admission gates pass. The backfill marker is keyed by the stored thread `sessionId`, not the stable route session key, so a real `/new` or session reset in a thread gets its own recovery fetch while same-session follow-ups avoid repeated server fetches.

When the first cold turn has no stored thread session entry yet, the monitor now records a pending backfill marker and adopts it once `recordInboundSessionMeta` creates the stored session id. That keeps the marker stable for same-session follow-ups and failed-fetch no-retry, without blocking a later real session-id rotation.

Backfilled sender labels use stable Mattermost user ids instead of per-post user lookups, keeping recovery bounded to the thread fetch path.

## User Impact

Mattermost thread replies keep useful prior context after restart or `/new`, without repeated thread-history requests or extra user lookup delays on normal same-session follow-ups.

## Evidence

- `pnpm vitest run extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts --reporter=verbose`: 72 passed; covers stored thread `sessionId` rotation, same-session no-refetch, failed-fetch no-retry, dropped pre-admission posts, bounded backfill without sender enrichment, and the initially-missing session entry path where a same-session follow-up must not refetch after a random stored `sessionId` is created.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Live proof: local Docker Mattermost Team Edition 10.11.21 at `http://localhost:8065`, with tokens and Mattermost ids redacted. The proof used real Mattermost REST auth, posts, and `/api/v4/posts/<root>/thread` through `monitorMattermostProvider`; a fake websocket only injected `posted` events into the monitor. The route/thread session key stayed stable while the stored thread `sessionId` rotated. Cold start included prior root/thread context, same-session server-only context stayed absent, and stored-thread-session reset included new server-only prior context:

```json
{
  "mattermost": "10.11.21 local Docker, token/id redacted",

  "threadSessionKey": "stable, redacted",
  "threadSessionKeyStable": true,

  "firstColdStartContainsRootContext": true,
```

target.title: fix(tool-call-repair): accept zero-parameter XML-ish function calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102933 — `parseXmlishPlainTextToolCallBlockAt` and
`parseXmlishPlainTextToolCallBlockEndAt` reject function calls with zero
parameters (e.g. `<function=get_system_info></function>`) by returning `null`
when `parameterCount === 0`. This prevents tool-call-repair from recognizing
or repairing any XML-ish tool calls that do not take arguments.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two `parameterCount === 0` guard clauses were overly conservative. The
existing close-tag validation (`consumeXmlishFunctionClose`) already
guarantees that a `</function>` delimiter is present before the block is
accepted. Removing the parameter count check allows zero-parameter calls to
reach the close-tag validator, which correctly handles the empty-body case.

## User Impact

**Before:** `<function=get_system_info></function>` → `parseStandalonePlainTextToolCallBlocks` returns `null`
**After:** Same input → returns `[{ name: "get_system_info", arguments: {} }]`

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/102933-zero-param-tool-call` | Base: `upstream/main` | Node: v22.19.0 Linux x64

### Regression tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.test.ts --reporter=verbose

```

### Live proof: node --import tsx

```
$ node --import tsx -e "..."
Before fix: null
After fix: [{name:"get_info",arguments:{},...}]
```

target.title: fix: preserve prompt cache continuity in embedded sessions
target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Long-lived embedded sessions could lose prompt-cache continuity in three connected ways:

- ambient `room_event` turns changed cache-visible delivery instructions and owner-only tool schemas;
- preflight, manual, and queued compaction rebuilt prompt/tool state from the current turn's delivery mode instead of the session-stable prompt mode;
- the built-in authenticated session stream was mistaken for a custom stream, so `openai-chatgpt-responses` runs used the managed full-context SSE adapter instead of OpenClaw's native cached WebSocket continuation path.

## Fix

- Separate effective source delivery from the session-stable prompt-facing delivery mode. Room events still require `message_tool_only` delivery without rewriting the cached prompt contract. Executable message tools retain the real turn mode, while Pi and Codex use the stable mode only for model-visible prompt/tool shape.
- Keep the safe room-event owner-only core-tool inventory stable across sender changes while preserving execution authorization.
- Carry the prompt-facing mode through primary runs, queued followups, Codex app-server prompt/tool builders, and every compaction entry point; compaction now rebuilds tools and system text from that stable mode. Codex keeps reusable thread instructions stable and adds strict room-event delivery guidance only to the current turn.
- Mark OpenClaw's built-in session auth wrapper and allow only that known wrapper to select the native `openai-chatgpt-responses` stream. Unmarked custom/provider streams retain their existing routing.

The native routing check is API-based, so it covers GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 without model-version branches.

## Evidence

Redacted same-session traces from the reported Discord room-event flow showed tool inventory flipping between 44 and 47 tools and cache reads collapsing to roughly 2k-10k or ceilinging around 37k-40k. With the room-event prompt/tool fix installed, warm turns with stable inventory reached roughly 49k-52k cached tokens on approximately 51k-55k context.

The route regression test reproduces the built-in auth-wrapper misclassification. A two-turn GPT-5.6 Sol WebSocket test then proves that the native provider sends the second turn with `previous_response_id` and only the new input, rather than replaying the full context.

## Validation

Validated at head `f0d85b0829d54ec9f3bda3406168f8bf2d8c0d6d` on upstream `main` `8dedb0ebcaef2bbe6dcd7b9ad137554b62ac1d21`:

- focused regression suite: 25 project test files, 1,211 tests passed, including a real targetless room-event send through the internal source-reply sink;
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`, `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm tsgo:test:packages`, and the 120-plugin extension package boundary compile passed;
- changed TypeScript passed `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint`; all generated prompt snapshots are current;
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.

## Boundaries

- Effective room-event delivery remains strict; this does not make private final text visible.
- Non-owner execution of owner-only tools remains blocked.
- Custom provider/session streams are not rerouted.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
